intro: Looking for fleet insurance near you usually means you run several vehicles for a business and want them covered under one arrangement rather than a patchwork of separate policies. You may be adding vans, cars or larger vehicles as the business grows, or finding that renewing each one individually has become a chore. iComply is a free introduction service: tell us what you need and we introduce you to a UK insurance broker who can quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for fleet insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search are business owners or fleet managers who want one policy that fits how their vehicles are actually used.
needs: You run a small business with a handful of vans or cars and want them covered under a single fleet policy instead of renewing each vehicle separately.
Your fleet has grown beyond the point where individual policies make sense, and you want to understand how fleet cover would work for your mix of vehicles.
You employ or use several drivers and need a broker to explain how driver policies and named driver arrangements affect your cover.
You want to talk to someone local or easily reachable about your vehicles, rather than dealing with a call centre.
You are reviewing your cover at renewal and want to know whether telematics or other options could suit how your vehicles are driven.
context_heading: Understanding fleet cover and who can arrange it
context: Fleet insurance covers several business vehicles on one policy, which can simplify admin and often reduce cost. Fleet size thresholds vary between insurers, so what counts as a fleet for one may not for another, and a broker can tell you where your vehicles would sit.

Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the type and number of vehicles in your fleet, as this shapes which brokers can help.
Describe what the vehicles are used for, such as deliveries, passenger transport or site work, and whether they are kept overnight at a business address.
Say who drives the vehicles, including employees, family members or regular contractors, and whether any are under twenty-five.
Mention any claims or incidents involving your vehicles in recent years, as brokers will need this to seek quotes.
Explain whether you already hold fleet cover or separate policies, and when your renewal falls due.
Tell us where your business is based and how far you are willing to travel or deal remotely, since you searched for fleet insurance near me.
questions: What fleet size threshold applies to my vehicles, and would I qualify for a fleet policy?
How will the policy treat drivers who are not named, and what is your approach to driver policies?
What excesses apply, and how do they differ between vehicles and drivers?
Would telematics be worth considering for my fleet, and how would it affect the cover?
Which key exclusions should I be aware of for the way my vehicles are used?
How are you paid for arranging this policy, and what happens if I need to complain?

faqs.q: Do I need a minimum number of vehicles for fleet insurance?
faqs.a: Fleet size thresholds vary between insurers, so there is no single number that applies everywhere. A broker can tell you whether your vehicles would be accepted as a fleet or whether separate policies would suit you better.

faqs.q: Can fleet insurance cover drivers who are not named on the policy?
faqs.a: Driver policies matter, and how unnamed or occasional drivers are treated depends on the insurer and the policy terms. Ask the broker to explain exactly who is covered and under what conditions before you commit.

faqs.q: Would telematics help my business vehicles?
faqs.a: Telematics can help by giving insight into how vehicles are driven, and some insurers take it into account. Whether it benefits you depends on your fleet and how it is used, so raise it with the broker when you speak.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. You can also ask whether they belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association or hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

extra_heading: Fleet cover versus insuring each vehicle separately
extra: People searching for fleet insurance near me are often weighing up whether to move away from insuring each vehicle on its own policy. Separate policies can mean several renewal dates, several sets of paperwork and several excesses to keep track of, while a fleet arrangement brings the vehicles together under one policy. The right answer depends on how many vehicles you run and how they are used, which is exactly what a broker will want to discuss.

It is worth being clear that fleet cover is not simply a discount for having more than one vehicle. Insurers set their own thresholds for what they will treat as a fleet, and the terms can differ in how they handle drivers, excesses and claims. A broker can compare how your vehicles would sit under a fleet policy against keeping them separate, so you can judge which arrangement suits your business rather than assuming one is always better.

Because you searched for fleet insurance near me, you may also value being able to sit down with someone or speak to the same person each time. Ask the broker how they would handle a claim involving one of your vehicles, who you would contact, and whether they deal with fleets of your size and type. That conversation tells you more about fit than any description of cover alone.

extra_faqs.q: Is fleet insurance always cheaper than separate policies?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Whether a fleet policy works out better depends on your vehicles, drivers and claims history, and insurers price these differently. Ask the broker to explain the comparison for your circumstances rather than assuming one route is cheaper.

extra_faqs.q: What happens at a first conversation with a fleet insurance broker?
extra_faqs.a: Expect questions about your vehicles, what they are used for, who drives them and any claims history, followed by an explanation of how fleet cover would work for you. The broker should set out key features, exclusions and how they are paid before you decide whether to proceed.

extra_faqs.q: Can I move my existing vehicles onto a fleet policy mid-term?
extra_faqs.a: That depends on your current policies and their terms, so raise it with the broker before making any change. They can explain what cancelling or amending existing cover would involve and whether a fleet arrangement could start at a sensible point for you.
